Build simple, readable, maintainable code with single-responsibility modules, clear interfaces, separated concerns, meaningful names, consistent style and 2-space indentation. Apply SOLID; document reusable components. Avoid duplicating logic and functionality across multiple files. Avoid over-engineering solutions. Only implement functionality that is currently required. Don't introduce features or code that is not explicitly needed.

Use clear file names; include a README overview and instructions. Comment complex logic judiciously; add docstrings to all functions, classes, and modules. Keep files under 180 lines and functions/classes ideally under 60 lines. Avoid unnecessary statements or blank lines.

Minimum: 80% code coverage. Test critical functionality with unit tests and integration tests. Write testable code; refactor regularly and review the codebase.

Define clear interfaces for agent creation, deployment, and monitoring. Implement robust data validation and error handling. Design communication mechanisms (e.g., message queues) for agent interaction. Consider security implications when designing agent functionality.
